purpose: agy-domain-skeptic proposed a cheap validation: across 8 sensor channels x 8 crops (64 cells), count the cells holding a value explicitly labelled as an optimum rather than a disease-risk, experimental, or stage-specific condition. Its stated prediction was '<= 10 of 64, and all of them are air_temperature or soil_pH'. The moderator executed this directly rather than taking any agent's word for it, because the result decides whether the product is viable as specified.
method: Each crop document ends with a '작물별 최종 요약 양식' (per-crop final summary) block — the most normalised part of the corpus. The sensor-relevant axes were extracted from that block for all 8 crops verbatim, then cross-checked against crop_evidence_gaps_6_crops.json.

corpus_scale_finding.interpretation: The corpus contains 674 explicit refusals to state a value. Absence is not an edge case in this data — it is the majority state. Any schema that models absence as NULL or as a missing row is modelling the dominant fact type as an exception.

air_humidity.evidence: All 8 crops record optimum RH as absent, verbatim: basil '생육 최적 RH 직접 근거 없음', peppermint '직접 확인된 최적 수치 없음', cherry_tomato/welsh_onion/arugula/lettuce/coriander '직접 근거 없음', wasabi '성체 최적 RH 없음' (its 90-95% figure is a propagation rooting condition, not adult cultivation).
air_humidity.note: Confirms the council's unanimous position. Every RH number in the corpus is a disease-risk or propagation condition.

soil_moisture.evidence: basil/peppermint/welsh_onion/lettuce/coriander have no universal sensor value at all. The three crops that do have numbers are all measurement-locked: cherry_tomato 'VWC 0.319/0.330 m3/m3 in a specific medium, explicitly not universal', arugula 'VWC 0.30 m3/m3 on a specific FDR sensor and medium', wasabi '>=95% of field capacity, a facility proposal'. Three different measurement bases, none matching a generic capacitive probe.

soil_temperature.verdict: STAGE-SPECIFIC ONLY — germination is the only supported phase
soil_temperature.evidence: basil/peppermint/wasabi record '직접 근거 없음'. The remaining five have germination-only values: cherry_tomato 23.9-29.4 C germination, welsh_onion 13-20 C germination, arugula 30 C germination optimum, lettuce 12.8-18.3 C germination, coriander ~24.83 C germination. Every one is explicitly marked as not a whole-cycle value.

illuminance.evidence: Not a single lux figure exists in the corpus. Light evidence is PPFD, DLI, shading percentage, or hours. Three crops give hour counts (basil 6-8 h/day, peppermint min 3 h/day, arugula 4-6 h/day) but a lux sensor cannot produce 'hours of bright light' without a brightness threshold that the corpus never defines. Three crops say '전일광' (full sun) with no hour value; welsh_onion and wasabi record '직접 근거 없음'.

air_temperature.verdict: THE ONLY PARTIALLY SCORABLE AXIS — and it is narrower than the council assumed

per_crop.caveat: Literature-cited optimum. Explicitly not a day/night split and explicitly not an alarm line.
None found beyond the corpus-wide absence of duration data.

per_crop.value: 12.2-15 C (WSU ideal); other sources prefer 8-18 C
per_crop.caveat: Two overlapping ranges from different sources; needs a curation decision.
DOWNGRADED: the registry flags this as general_crop_reference AND not_a_risk_threshold — it is a general protected-cultivation range, not a lettuce-specific validated optimum.

CATEGORY ERROR RISK: this is a 일평균 (DAILY MEAN) figure. Comparing an instantaneous sensor reading to a daily-mean optimum is exactly the kind of conflation the documents warn against. Scoring it requires aggregating to a daily mean first.
'고유 범용값 없음'. Only a general tomato fruit-set reference (day 15.6-32.2 C, night 15.6-23.9 C), flagged general_crop_reference in the registry.
'주야 범용 직접값 없음'. Only qualitative: cool-season crop.

headline.prediction: agy-domain-skeptic predicted <=10 of 64 cells would qualify, all air_temperature or soil_pH.
headline.scorable_cell_count: 3 solidly (basil, peppermint, wasabi air temperature), 4 with an explicit caveat (adding lettuce as a general-crop reference), 5 only if welsh_onion is first aggregated to a daily mean. Out of 64 cells. Every other axis is 0.
headline.most_important_consequence: THREE OF THE EIGHT MVP CROPS — cherry tomato, arugula, and coriander — have NO scorable axis whatsoever. Not a weak one: zero. For those crops an 'environment score' cannot be computed from any of the 8 sensor channels without fabricating a number. This is a product-definition problem, not a schema problem, and it was not visible in the brief.

implications_for_the_debate: The council's convergence on 'air temperature is the scorable axis' is empirically correct but was stated too generously. Air temperature is scorable for 3-4 crops, not for crops in general.

welsh_onion's daily-mean range is a new instance of the corpus's central hazard (comparing incommensurable measurement bases) that no agent caught. It supports the argument that measurement basis must be structural, not conventional.

674 explicit absence markers means 'no direct evidence' is the corpus's dominant value. This strongly supports codex-evidence-modeler's position that absence needs first-class representation and NULL is inadequate, and undercuts any wide-table design.

The 3-crops-with-zero-scorable-axes finding is the strongest available argument for agy-domain-skeptic's reframing: the product cannot honestly be 'an environment score dashboard' for all 8 crops. It can be a condition monitor that scores where evidence exists and advises everywhere else.
This finding must be put in front of agy-product-advocate and agy-skeptic when they run, since it directly determines what dashboard is buildable and how much schema is justified.
limits_of_this_validation: It reads the per-crop final summary block, which is a distillation. A value could exist in the body but be omitted from the summary. Spot-checks against basil sections 2-5 and the registry did not surface such a case, but the check is not exhaustive.
It assesses only the 8 hardware channels. Axes such as soil pH and EC do have direct evidence (e.g. basil pH 6.0-7.5) but no sensor reports them in the current hardware set.
It is corpus-bound. Whether the researchers were right to exclude broader horticultural references is outside its scope.
